Priya: FYI pushed a small docs PR updating streaming pagination snippets to the new API (old client.streamPages -> client.stream_pages). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4933 :memo:
SnippetBot: PR #4933 created by Priya  snippet-checker failed: missing 'await' in python async iterator example. Check logs: https://ci.redwood-inference/pipelines/4933/logs :warning:
Tom: thanks for flagging. i'll fix the await. i also noticed the TS example uses page.chunks but the new API returns items. need to update that across files.
Hannah: quick thought  can we keep backward-compatible aliases in the snippet text? i.e., show "client.stream_pages (formerly streamPages)" footnote. avoids churn for older posts.
Priya: i'd prefer changing examples to canonical new names and add a short migration note at the top. easier to maintain. older aliases in code are confusing.
Ben: QA-Bot ran link check and found one broken internal link in the 'Best practices' anchor (broken due to heading rename). i'll open a tiny follow-up to fix anchors.
Priya: thanks. Tom, do you want me to push the await/TS fixes or do you have them?
Tom: i'll send a patch in a minute. Python fix is trivial  forgot to await the async generator next call. also adding a comment about client-side retry helper.
Priya: paste the fixed snippets here so i can sanity-check before you push.
Tom: python fixed snippet:
```python
async def stream_pages(client, start_cursor=None):
    cursor = start_cursor
    while True:
        # retry_with_backoff is our helper for transient errors
        resp = await retry_with_backoff(lambda: client.get_page(cursor=cursor, page_size=16))
        async for chunk in resp.stream():
            process(chunk)
            # yield control to event loop to apply backpressure
            await asyncio.sleep(0)
        if not resp.next_cursor:
            break
        cursor = resp.next_cursor
```
Hannah: looks good. small nit: use page_size=32 in examples to match other pages in docs. also change function name to match sdk style (stream_pages -> stream_pages_async).
Tom: updated. TS snippet (fixed):
```ts
for await (const page of client.stream_pages({ pageSize: 32 })) {
  for (const item of page.items) {
    handleChunk(item)
    // attach backpressure logic here (pause/resume consumer)
  }
}
```
Ben: i'm running snippet-runner locally and re-ran the linter. two small issues: (1) go example missing error handling around stream termination, (2) markdown fenced blocks missing language tag in one spot. i'll open a tiny docs CI PR for the md lint rule enforcement.
Priya: good catch. not a blocker for merge but please fix before we publish.
QA-Bot: snippet-runner results: python example passes after await fix; ts passes after items rename; go example failed: missing defer close on response. See details: https://ci.redwood-inference/pipelines/4933/snippet-runner
Tom: i'll add Go fix now. Go patch (draft):
```go
func StreamPages(ctx context.Context, client *redwood.Client, cursor string) error {
  for {
    resp, err := client.GetPage(ctx, &redwood.PageRequest{Cursor: cursor, PageSize: 32})
    if err != nil {
      return err
    }
    defer resp.Body.Close() // ensure resources freed per page
    for _, i := range resp.Items {
      fmt.Println(i.Text)
    }
    if resp.NextCursor == "" {
      break
    }
    cursor = resp.NextCursor
  }
  return nil
}
```
Hannah: tiny suggestion: move defer resp.Body.Close() immediately after resp, not inside loop body after processing, to avoid accumulating defers. also mention ctx timeouts.
Tom: good point. i'll adjust.
Priya: cool. once you push Tom, i'll request a review from docs-owners and merge after CI. Ben, QA follow-up for the anchor fix + lint rule is fine as separate PR.
Ben: filed docs PR #4934 to add md-lint enforcement and fix the anchor. linking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4934 :link:
Priya: thanks everyone. merging once new CI run is green. will add a short migration blurb at the top of the page explaining streamPages -> stream_pages and items vs chunks.
Tom: done and pushed. tagging reviewers now. :rocket:
